principles.text: When the leaders are vertical (90-degree, consecutive green days, far above the 50 EMA), don't be aggressive; shift focus to taking profits rather than opening new positions.
Exit weak/extended positions one by one, slowly and steadily, rather than dumping everything at once, so you keep some exposure to capture the final leg if the run continues.
Sell into strength on discretion; don't wait for a close below the 9 EMA, because the fastest movers get too extended and a post-9EMA-close exit can cost a ~20% pullback.

On margin with heavy long exposure, prefer trimming early and re-buying on a fresh breakout over sitting through a pullback, because a correction hits all correlated positions at once and amplifies drawdown from the peak.
Don't short too early: when you start to feel bearish, the market usually pushes a few more days/weeks higher before the real reversal. It's too early to short and too late to long.
The same chart in a different context/timing yields a different decision; situational awareness governs whether to take an otherwise-clean breakout. In a stretched market, skip new breakouts.
